projects.title: RENEW
projects.summary: Empowering communities to save energy, reduce carbon, and embrace renewables.
intro: Empowering citizens to become prosumers — individuals who both produce and consume renewable energy — through education, engagement, and accessible digital tools.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: The main goal of RENEW is to encourage carbon reduction, increase renewable energy adoption, and improve energy efficiency at the local level. By connecting technology, awareness, and participation, RENEW helps communities take ownership of their energy future.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: The project aims to create a replicable model for sustainable energy communities, demonstrating how digital innovation can drive both environmental and social benefits — paving the way for a cleaner, more resilient Europe.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: Through interactive dashboards, learning modules, and real-time data visualization, RENEW supports citizens in managing their energy production and consumption effectively.

The platform is designed to be intuitive and inclusive — accessible to both younger audiences learning about sustainability and older users who may be less familiar with digital technologies. By combining simplicity with educational value, RENEW makes renewable energy understandable and engaging for everyone.

projects.title: RES4CITY
projects.summary: Advancing sustainable cities through education, innovation, and renewable energy.
intro: RES4CITY drives sustainable urban transformation through innovation, education, and technology.
The project promotes renewable energy adoption, resource circularity, and low-carbon solutions tailored for cities and densely populated areas — building the foundation for a greener, smarter future.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: The main goal of RES4CITY is to strengthen sustainable renewable energy and fuel technologies within urban areas. The project focuses on promoting sustainability, circularity, and innovative education designed together with stakeholders. By developing highly skilled human capital, RES4CITY supports the widespread adoption of renewable solutions across different educational systems.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: RES4CITY aims to create a scalable framework that accelerates the deployment of renewable energy technologies in cities. With increasing resource consumption in densely populated areas, the project provides tools and knowledge that support low-carbon urban development and contribute directly to Europe's green transition.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: With a consortium of 18 partners across eight EU countries and Switzerland, RES4CITY works to close the skills gap in renewable energy and circularity.
The project combines research, education, and innovation to prepare professionals capable of driving sustainable change in modern cities.

projects.title: FLOW
projects.summary: Boosting smart EV charging and seamless V2X integration into energy systems.
intro: FLOW boosts and demonstrates multifaceted EV smart charging and V2X integration into energy systems.

It provides user-centric, interoperable solutions for seamless energy exchange between vehicles, buildings, and the grid — optimising operations, enhancing grid flexibility, and supporting large-scale decarbonisation.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: FLOW boosts and demonstrates multifaceted EV smart charging and V2X integration into energy systems thanks to a range of comprehensive solutions providing answers to the needs of all actors involved.

These solutions include highly replicable user-centric products, concepts, configurations and mechanisms to optimise operation. Cross-sector harmonisation and standardisation is delivered to facilitate activities of stakeholders and EV users.

Advanced interoperable solutions enhance planning, operation and assessment of EV charging for seamless integration into the energy system and identification of the most appropriate scenario based on a multi-criteria model, leveraging appropriate business models and tailored services.
FLOW also delivers multi-actor orchestration to ensure data exchange and synchronisation across actors for VGI and EV flexibility services.

These solutions are deployed in 5 demonstrations (including 2 testbeds and 3 large-scale demos) in CZ, IE, IT, DK, and ES covering a wide range of applications (e.g., V1G/V2B/V2H/V2G, public/private/semi-public, urban/rural/touristic, car/small- & medium-commerce) to validate and quantify the benefits associated with enabling and valorising EV flexibility, alleviating grid challenges, and fostering mobility and energy decarbonization.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: Expected impacts include GHG emission reduction of 6 MtCO2eq/y, grid reinforcement saving up to 13 B€/country, increase local RES by 14% and avoid RES curtailment by 41 TWh.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: The consortium includes 26 partners from 9 European countries covering the entire value chain, including OEM, technology providers, CPOs, aggregators, DSOs, TSO, ICT developers, RTOs experts in users, mobility, harmonisation, optimisation tools, energy integration and leveraging the networks of umbrella associations from the electromobility and the DSOs.
These ensure replicability and scalability to foster the EV penetration trends, thanks also to comprehensive communication, dissemination and exploitation actions.

projects.title: SHERLOCK
projects.summary: Upskilling professionals with green and digital skills for building renovation.
intro: SHERLOCK designs and implements an innovative educational framework based on microcredentials to upskill the workforce and promote lifelong learning.
It focuses on green and digital skills for the building renovation sector, bridging the gap between education, finance, and energy efficiency to support the EU decarbonisation goals.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: The SHERLOCK project aims to boost innovation at European level by designing and implementing an original and advanced educational framework based on microcredentials for upskilling the workforce and lifelong learning.

It will integrate and combine a multidisciplinary green and digital skills portfolio to foster cooperation and knowledge exchange across stakeholders, supporting job creation and the EU's mass energy building retrofitting targets. SHERLOCK addresses the urgent need for a skilled workforce capable of managing the technical, financial and societal aspects of building energy retrofitting.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: The project contributes to the EU decarbonisation goals by 2050, addressing the building sector which accounts for 40% of energy consumption and 35% of carbon emissions.

By equipping professionals with green and digital skills, SHERLOCK helps bridge the gap between financial operators and energy project developers, ensuring a skilled workforce for the building renovation wave.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: SHERLOCK will develop and deliver a MOOC-based MicroMaster programme and a VET-oriented training course designed with stakeholders and VET providers. The project will establish SHERLOCK Knowledge Centres as long-term hubs for collaboration between universities, businesses, and public institutions.
It will define learning objectives, design materials, and produce guidelines for educators on implementing innovative MicroMaster programmes that support lifelong learning and workforce upskilling.

projects.title: STREACS
projects.summary: Enhancing Armenia's research capacity for clean and secure energy transition.
intro: STREACS strengthens Armenia's research capacity to accelerate the transition toward clean and renewable energy while enhancing energy security.
It fosters collaboration and knowledge exchange between Armenian and European institutions to support sustainable energy development.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: STREACS aims to enhance Armenia's research capacity to accelerate the country's transition toward clean and renewable energy, while ensuring energy security.

The project supports the implementation of the European Green Deal by promoting a sustainable, decarbonised, and resilient energy system adapted to Armenia's specific geopolitical and technical context.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: By strengthening research capacity and fostering cooperation, STREACS contributes to Armenia's long-term decarbonisation and energy transition goals.
It enables better integration of Armenia into the European Research Area and enhances its ability to produce innovative, sustainable energy solutions through shared expertise and best practices.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: STREACS facilitates the transfer of knowledge and exchange of best practices between research institutions, universities, and partners across the EU.
The project builds networks for academic and policy collaboration, supporting Armenia in developing clean-energy research and innovation aligned with European standards.

projects.title: AI-EFFECT
projects.summary: Advancing reliable AI applications for Europe's clean energy future.
intro: AI-EFFECT establishes a European hub for testing and validating AI solutions in the energy sector — ensuring interoperability, trust, and compliance with the EU AI Act.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: AI-EFFECT aims to establish a European Testing and Experimentation Facility (TEF) for developing, testing, and validating AI applications in the energy sector.

The project connects existing facilities into a distributed digital platform to foster interoperability, flexibility, and scalability, becoming a central hub for collaboration across utilities, academia, and regulatory authorities.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: AI-EFFECT strengthens Europe's capacity for safe, interoperable, and certified AI technologies in the energy domain.
It promotes transparency, data integrity, and cross-sector innovation while aligning with the EU AI Act and Energy Data Spaces to ensure trustworthy and sustainable AI adoption.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: The project develops and tests AI-driven use cases for district heating, grid congestion, distributed energy integration, and energy communities.
The consortium designs governance, certification, and business models ensuring AI-EFFECT's long-term sustainability beyond EU funding.

projects.title: RESSKILL
projects.summary: Building skills for Europe's sustainable and digital energy future.
intro: RESSKILL empowers Europe's workforce with AI-driven, gamified education and microcredentials to accelerate the green and digital energy transition.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: The RESSKILL project is a comprehensive and transformative initiative strategically positioned to catapult the European Union into a more sustainable and resilient future. RESSKILL places a critical emphasis on human capital, understanding that skilled professionals are integral to achieving a sustainable energy future.

Going beyond traditional educational efforts, the project is a multifaceted endeavor designed to meet the evolving needs of the renewable energy sector, with a specific focus on energy system integration and digitalisation for buildings and districts. This aligns with the broader vision of creating intelligent, energy-efficient urban spaces.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: By investing in skills, knowledge, and digital proficiency, the project is steering the EU towards a more sustainable, energy-efficient, and technologically advanced future.

RESSKILL incorporates Artificial Intelligence (AI) for skill needs identification, to ensure that the educational programs are dynamically tailored to the evolving demands of the construction industry, making the workforce not just competent but also agile in response to changing technologies and requirements.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: A distinctive feature of RESSKILL is the development of Micro Credentials, providing tangible validation of an individual's expertise and ensuring alignment with industry standards. Case study education, based on real-world scenarios and success stories, is adopted to ensure that the workforce emerging from the RESSKILL program can apply theoretical concepts in practical situations.

By incorporating gamification, RESSKILL transforms the educational process into an immersive and enjoyable journey, fostering a deeper understanding and retention of complex concepts. RESSKILL is not merely an educational initiative; it is a dynamic and adaptive force, leveraging AI, gamification, and case study education to empower the workforce.

projects.title: NEXSYS
projects.summary: Advancing energy modelling and optimisation to achieve net-zero and sustainable living.
intro: NexSys advances research in energy modelling and optimisation to support the transition toward Net Zero Carbon Energy Systems and sustainable living.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: The energy system is a vital pillar of national infrastructure in all economies, and the research in this programme entails advanced modelling and optimisation of this system, investigating its future development and role in addressing the major energy challenges which face society.

The research programme is firmly within the energy field, addressing some of the major engineering research questions within the field of power and energy engineering, with the potential to significantly advance the state of the art and, through mathematical modelling, deliver key new insights into the challenges surrounding the decarbonisation of energy systems and pathways to the achievement of Net Zero Carbon Energy Systems.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: The programme also draws together a diverse range of disciplines to tackle the challenge of net zero from a technical, economic, and social point of view.
This interdisciplinary approach aims to provide a deeper understanding of decarbonisation pathways and contribute to the achievement of sustainable, net-zero energy systems.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: In line with SFI's legal remit, the NexSys research programme comprises oriented basic research in the hub with complementary applied research in the targeted projects fully aligned with the Energy, Climate Action and Sustainability Refreshed Priority Theme, covering both the priority areas Decarbonising the Energy System and Sustainable Living.

projects.title: ADFLEX
projects.summary: Enabling communities to enhance energy flexibility, validate smart solutions, and accelerate renewables integration.
intro: ADFLEX develops and validates smart energy solutions that enhance flexibility, integrate digital technologies, and empower Sustainable Energy Communities to participate in local energy markets.

sections.heading: Objective
paragraphs: The ADFLEX project addresses key challenges in supporting Sustainable Energy Communities to provide energy flexibility and participate in local energy markets within mixed-use buildings. It integrates expertise from energy management, digital technology, and stakeholder engagement to develop an integrated, scalable solution validated through on-site pilot testing.

sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: ADFLEX contributes to national and EU energy goals by reducing emissions, enhancing renewable energy penetration, and improving grid flexibility at distribution and transmission levels. Its outcomes aim to accelerate the clean-energy transition and deliver high-impact, scalable results for communities across Europe.

sections.heading: Our Role
paragraphs: ADFLEX brings together partners and stakeholders to co-develop and implement digital tools and smart energy frameworks that enhance coordination between communities, DSOs and TSOs. Through collaboration and validation within the Ringsend Sustainable Energy Community, the project ensures robust, real-world testing of its solutions.

publications.title: Demand response algorithms for smart-grid ready residential buildings using machine learning models
publications.description: This paper assesses the performance of control algorithms for the implementation of demand response strategies in the residential sector. A typical house, representing the most common building category in Ireland, was fully instrumented and utilised as a test-bed.

publications.title: On the assessment and control optimisation of demand response programs in residential buildings
publications.description: The ability to control and optimise energy consumption at end-user level is of increasing interest as a means to achieve a balance between supply and demand, particularly when large penetration of distributed renewable energy sources is being considered.

publications.title: Diversification, concentration and renewability of the energy supply in the European Union
publications.description: Energy security assessment quantifies the energy supply to a population and the likelihood, or risk, of an energy disruption or shortage and represents an important aspect of national security, economic stability and prosperity. The quantification of the state of energy supply is context-dependent and involves multiple perspectives: infrastructural, technological, environmental, market, social and geopolitical. Among all the different and relevant aspects involved, diversity and dependence of the energy fuel mix are two of the main energy security dimensions.

publications.title: Forecast electricity demand in commercial building with machine learning models to enable demand response programs
publications.description: Electricity load forecasting is an important part of power system dispatching. Accurately forecasting electricity load have great impact on a number of departments in power systems. Compared to electricity load simulation (white-box model), electricity load forecasting (black-box model) does not require expertise in building construction. The development cycle of the electricity load forecasting model is much shorter than the design cycle of the electricity load simulation.

publications.title: Artificial Intelligence Enabled Demand Response: Prospects and Challenges in Smart Grid Environment
publications.description: Demand Response (DR) has gained popularity in recent years as a practical strategy to increase the sustainability of energy systems while reducing associated costs. Despite this, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), have recently developed as critical technologies for demand-side management and response due to the high complexity of tasks associated with DR, as well as huge amount of data management to take decisions very near to real time implications.

publications.title: Review on recent optimization strategies for hybrid renewable energy system with hydrogen technologies: State of the art, trends and future directions
publications.description: The world is currently facing a power shortage due to the inadequacy of conventional energy sources and increased energy requirements in almost all sectors of human life. To mitigate this issue, the researchers have taken the considerable interest of researchers over the past decade in enhancing energy efficiency and viability.

publications.title: A survey on IoT-enabled smart grids: emerging, applications, challenges, and outlook
publications.description: Swift population growth and rising demand for energy in the 21st century have resulted in considerable efforts to make the electrical grid more intelligent and responsive to accommodate consumers' needs better while enhancing the reliability and efficiency of modern power systems. Internet of Things (IoT) has appeared as one of the enabling technologies for smart energy grids by delivering abundant cutting-edge solutions in various domains, including critical infrastructures.

publications.title: Optimal GWCSO-based home appliances scheduling for demand response considering end-users comfort
publications.description: Nowadays, the most notable uncertainty for an electricity utility lies in the electrical demand and generation in power systems. Demand response (DR) accomplishment due to the home appliances energy management has acquired considerable attention for the reliable and cost-optimized power grid.

publications.title: Investigating the indirect impact of transformational leadership on performance and work alienation: evidence from school principals navigating COVID-19
publications.description: Although significant research has examined the concept of transformational leadership, few studies have explored the indirect impact of transformational leadership on individual and organizational outcomes within the context of crisis. Accordingly, this study aims to advance our understanding of the indirect impact of transformational leadership on school performance and principals' work alienation within the context of the COVID-19 pandemic.

publications.title: Interrogating illusions of progress: citizen science, science communication, and a call for inclusive reform
publications.description: With their foundations in Ancient Greek symposia, progression to eighteenth-century French salons and coffeehouses, up to modern incarnations of large-scale international meetings, conferences have a rich history of bringing scholars together to communicate new views, opinions, and research findings (Nicolson, 2017; Roche, 2022).

publications.title: A hybrid Gaussian process-integrated deep learning model for retrofitted building energy optimization in smart city ecosystems
publications.description: Traditional retrofitting methods need a considerable upgrade; therefore, they often require significant time and financial investment, and can disrupt the building operations and occupant activities during implementation. Consequently, developing fast-response retrofitting solutions to save energy on urban and large scales is critical for city planners and policymakers.

publications.title: A National Study of Irish Leadership in STEM Education
publications.description: This study draws on AMO framework to explore principals' perceptions of leadership in STEM education in addition to their role as leaders within their schools. This study addresses the following research question: How do principals influence or promote STEM education? An online survey instrument was administered to 3200 Irish Elementary School Principals.

news.title: Celebrating Science Night at Maynooth University!
news.author: Paolo Cammardella
news.summary: The IRESI Group and School of Business Maynooth University staff and students were delighted to host a stand for Science Night.

paragraphs: The IRESI Group and [School of Business Maynooth University](https://www.linkedin.com/company/school-of-business-maynooth-university/) staff and students were delighted to host a stand for Science Night organised by [Maynooth University](https://www.linkedin.com/company/maynooth-university/) on November 15th. It was a fantastic evening dedicated to inspiring future generations about the wonders of science and their potential to shape a sustainable future.

At our stand, we focused on renewable energy and its vital role in achieving net-zero carbon emissions. Through hands-on activities and engaging discussions, we aimed to empower families with the knowledge that their actions can make a real difference in combating climate change and building a greener planet. 🌍✨
A big thank you to Maynooth University for organizing such an impactful event and to all the young minds who visited us, brimming with curiosity and enthusiasm! 😊
Let's keep inspiring and innovating for a brighter, more sustainable future 💡

With [Fabiano Pallonetto](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fabianopallonetto/), [Amy Fahy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amy-fahy-7236baba/), [Carrie Anne Barry](https://www.linkedin.com/in/carrie-anne-barry-9b192616/), [Nicky Dawkins](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicky-dawkins-0b895b212/), [Annalisa Bringiotti](https://www.linkedin.com/in/annalisa-bringiotti-8509b8232/), [Pietro Luigi Desole](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pietro-luigi-desole-940148292/) and [Christina Barry](https://www.linkedin.com/in/christina-barry-6ab734304/).

news.title: Celebrating Sustainability and Stakeholder Engagement at the Kildare Business Awards!
news.author: Paolo Cammardella
news.summary: The IRESI group at School of Business Maynooth University was proud to represent the RENEWchallenge Project at the prestigious Kildare Business Awards.

paragraphs: The IRESI group at [School of Business Maynooth University](https://www.linkedin.com/company/school-of-business-maynooth-university/) was proud to represent the [RENEWchallenge](https://www.linkedin.com/company/renewchallenge/) Project at the prestigious Kildare Business Awards, where we were nominated in the Decarbonization Category.

The RENEW Project stands out for its dedication to stakeholder engagement, fostering collaboration to address critical challenges in energy transition and decarbonization. This recognition highlights the collective efforts of our team and partners in building a more sustainable future.

We were delighted to have our leadership team in attendance, including our guest of honor [Joseph Coughlan](https://www.linkedin.com/in/joseph-coughlan-016276b/), Head of School; [Fabiano Pallonetto](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fabianopallonetto/), our Director; [Amy Fahy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amy-fahy-7236baba/), our Vice Director; along with [Nicky Dawkins](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicky-dawkins-0b895b212/), our Lab Manager; [Carrie Anne Barry](https://www.linkedin.com/in/carrie-anne-barry-9b192616/), COER's Lab Manager; [Rebecca Doolin](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rebecca-doolin-78aa175/), Vice President External Affairs; [Gordon Jamieson](https://www.linkedin.com/in/gjamieson/), Senior Development Manager; [Peter McNamara](https://www.linkedin.com/in/peter-mcnamara-2035ab9/), Dean of the Faculty of Social Science; and Peter Conlon, Director of [MaynoothWorks](https://www.linkedin.com/company/maynoothworks/).

A heartfelt thank you to everyone who has supported this project, and congratulations to all the nominees and winners who are driving positive change in their fields. Here's to continued collaboration and innovation for a greener tomorrow! 💚🌍

news.title: Fostering Creativity and Collaboration at Maynooth University!
news.author: Paolo Cammardella
news.summary: We’re thrilled to share that our Vice Director, Amy Fahy, Director Fabiano Pallonetto, and Lab Manager Nicky Dawkins hosted a co-creation workshop.

paragraphs: We're thrilled to share that our Vice Director, [Amy Fahy](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amy-fahy-7236baba/), Director [Fabiano Pallonetto](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fabianopallonetto/), and Lab Manager [Nicky Dawkins](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nicky-dawkins-0b895b212/) of the IRESI Group, recently hosted an engaging workshop at [School of Business Maynooth University](https://www.linkedin.com/company/school-of-business-maynooth-university/) as part of the [Creative Ireland](https://www.linkedin.com/company/creative-ireland/) Maynooth Climate Lab project. This session was focused on co-creation to drive innovative solutions for climate challenges.

Special thanks to [Christina Barry](https://www.linkedin.com/in/christina-barry-6ab734304/) and Philip O'Brien from the Creative Ireland project who shared their experiences of facilitating hands-on experiential learning workshops with local families, to explore concepts like sustainable energy, transport, circular economy, and biodiversity in a fun and interactive way.

The day ended on a festive and interactive note with a gingerbread-making competition! This unique activity brought participants together, fostering teamwork and showcasing how creativity can inspire collaboration in meaningful ways.
A heartfelt thank you to everyone who contributed to the success of this event. Your enthusiasm and ideas are driving forces in our mission for a more sustainable future.
*#Innovation #Sustainability #Collaboration #CreativeThinking #Leadership #MaynoothUniversity*
